name: Ethics, Fiduciary Duty and Suitability
description: Original practice questions on fiduciary duty, conflicts of interest, client profiling and communications.

cards.prompt: An investment adviser's fiduciary duty consists of which two broad components?

options: Duty of care and duty of loyalty
Duty of profit and duty of speed
Duty of confidentiality and duty of secrecy

cards.explanation: The SEC's 2019 interpretation describes a duty of care (best interest advice, best execution, monitoring) and a duty of loyalty (not placing the adviser's interest ahead of the client's, with full and fair disclosure of conflicts).
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: When an adviser has a conflict of interest, the adviser must:

options: Fully and fairly disclose it so the client can give informed consent, or eliminate it

cards.explanation: Disclosure must be specific enough for the client to understand the conflict and provide informed consent.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which of the following is the best first step in developing a client's investment policy?

options: Gather information about the client's objectives, constraints, and risk tolerance

cards.explanation: Know-your-client information (goals, time horizon, liquidity needs, taxes, legal constraints, risk tolerance and capacity) drives the suitability analysis.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Risk tolerance differs from risk capacity in that tolerance is:

options: The client's financial ability to bear loss
The client's psychological willingness to bear loss

cards.explanation: Willingness is attitudinal; capacity is financial. The more conservative of the two typically governs.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A client who is 28 and saving for retirement in 35+ years generally has a:

options: Short time horizon and low risk capacity
Long time horizon, supporting higher equity allocation

cards.explanation: Long horizons allow more volatility; the adviser still considers risk tolerance and liquidity needs.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A retired client who needs reliable monthly income and has low risk tolerance is most appropriately offered:

options: Diversified, income-oriented holdings of higher quality with liquidity

cards.explanation: Recommendations must match the client's objectives, risk tolerance and cash-flow needs.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Churning is:

options: Excessive trading to generate commissions or fees that is inconsistent with client objectives

cards.explanation: Excessive trading for the adviser's benefit violates the fiduciary duty and antifraud provisions.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Front-running is:

options: Buying for yourself ahead of a known client order
Asking the client for a deposit

cards.explanation: Trading ahead of client orders to profit from the expected price move is fraud and a breach of loyalty.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: An adviser may not do which of the following?
cards.explanation: Guaranteeing returns or promising no loss is fraudulent or misleading. Investment advice must be given with disclosure of risks.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Under Regulation S-P, an adviser must provide clients with:

options: A privacy notice at the start of the relationship and annually (unless exempt)

cards.explanation: Reg S-P requires initial and annual privacy notices (subject to an exception if no sharing outside the exceptions) and safeguards for customer records.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which communication would most likely be misleading?

options: Showing only the best-performing accounts without disclosing that it is a selection

cards.explanation: Selective presentation of performance (cherry-picking results) is misleading under the antifraud provisions and the marketing rule.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A client asks the adviser to keep the client's account details confidential. The adviser may disclose the information to:

options: Only as required by law or with consent, or as permitted for servicing the account

cards.explanation: Client information must be protected; disclosure is permitted with consent, to service providers under confidentiality, or when required by law.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Dual registrants (IAR and broker-dealer agent) must be especially careful because they can:

options: Face conflicts between commission-based and fee-based roles and must disclose which capacity they act in

cards.explanation: Disclosure of capacity and conflicts is required when the same person acts as both adviser and broker-dealer representative.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Under Regulation Best Interest (for broker-dealers), a recommendation must:

options: Be in the retail customer's best interest at the time made, without placing the broker's interest ahead of the customer

cards.explanation: Reg BI requires a duty of care, disclosure, conflict mitigation and compliance obligations when recommending securities to retail customers.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Form CRS (relationship summary) is delivered to:
cards.explanation: Advisers and broker-dealers deliver Form CRS to retail investors at the start of the relationship and when materially updated.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A power of attorney or discretionary authority lets an adviser:

options: Make investment decisions without prior client approval for each trade within the agreed scope

cards.explanation: Discretion must be documented in the client agreement, typically via limited trading authorization. It does not permit withdrawal for the adviser's own use.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which fee arrangement is the most common for advisers?

options: A percentage of assets under management

cards.explanation: Asset-based fees (e.g., 1% of AUM) are most common; fee disclosure and billing practices must be described in Form ADV Part 2A.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: If a client's circumstances change significantly (e.g., job loss), the adviser should:

options: Ignore it until the annual review
Reassess the client profile and update recommendations as needed

cards.explanation: Duty of care includes monitoring the relationship at a frequency consistent with the agreed scope of services.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Soft-dollar benefits must be:
cards.explanation: Soft-dollar practices and conflicts must be disclosed; benefits within the 28(e) safe harbor must help the adviser's decision-making for clients.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which of the following is a prohibited practice under the Uniform Securities Act for an IAR?

options: Borrowing money from a client (unless the client is a financial institution in the business of lending)

cards.explanation: NASAA model rules prohibit advisers from borrowing from clients (with limited exceptions) and require disclosure of conflicts such as personal trading.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Which document spells out the services, fees, and termination terms of an advisory relationship?
cards.explanation: The advisory contract defines the engagement; Part 2A discloses the firm; Part 2B discloses supervised persons.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: When a client wants an aggressive strategy that is inconsistent with the client's circumstances, the adviser should:

options: Explain risks, document the discussion, and decline if the strategy is not suitable

cards.explanation: Advice must be in the client's best interest; unsolicited client instructions can be accepted when the adviser documents them and the strategy is not otherwise prohibited.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: Books and records for an SEC-registered adviser generally must be kept for:

options: 5 years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry, the first 2 years in the office

cards.explanation: Rule 204-2 generally requires 5 years, with the first two years in an appropriate office of the adviser.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline

cards.prompt: A client's "capacity" for loss primarily depends on:
cards.explanation: Capacity is objective: resources, obligations and time to recover from losses.
cards.sourceRef: SEC Commission Interpretation Regarding Standard of Conduct for Investment Advisers (Release IA-5248, 2019); NASAA Series 65 content outline
